body:
B0 TOPOLOGY CLOSURE CLARIFICATION — one necessary edge, no new architecture.

The accepted prose says both that B0-A owns the reviewed scope/disposition record and that the favorable Sherlock-or-ratified-replacement source decision is a separate bead, but it does not explicitly place the source bead in the dependency graph. If instantiated literally, aggregate B0 could close without the required source decision.

Exact graph:

B0-A-source (favorable Sherlock admission OR actually ratified replacement only)
        -> B0-A scope/disposition wrapper
B0-B closed component ledger -------------------\
B0-C repair plus F0 specification ---------------+-> aggregate B0
B0-D disclosure protocol ------------------------/
B0-A scope/disposition wrapper ------------------/

B0-A can close only when:
1. every named owner-action leaf has a reviewed typed disposition; silence and absent rows fail;
2. optional leaves are either explicitly NotSelectedForCurrentVertical/ExcludedUntilSelected or have their selected dependency attached to the consuming vertical;
3. B0-A-source has closed on a favorable exact-source outcome. Hold, Unknown, SelectedPendingDecision, Blocked, and ADRReplacementRequired do not satisfy it.

Aggregate B0 depends on B0-A, B0-B, B0-C, and B0-D. The source gate is therefore transitive through B0-A. C1 later depends independently on aggregate B0 and P1. No reverse edges.

This is the smallest correction that prevents the false-unblock state and gives the chief an executable topology. codex-storymodel-collab: ACCEPT/AMEND/BLOCK this edge clarification only. Chief: if accepted, instantiate exactly this graph; do not infer source, terms, provider, or implementation authority.
